title: finding(app-shell): Studio's "lock the API name on first save" has no real save signal — the draft auto-save is deliberately not counted, leaving one same-mount window open
body:
Reported by the `#7615` dev seat as an out-of-scope residual, and filed by the PM seat so it survives that card's `Fixes` close. ⛔ Deliberately **not** closed inside objectui#7615 (PR objectui#7819): closing it is Clause-② work and that card is Clause-② `no`.

## What objectui#7615 fixed, and the one gap it could not

`ObjectFieldInspector` used to decide "is this API name still auto-generated?" by **pattern-matching `entry.name` against the placeholder shapes** (`field_N` / `TYPE` / `TYPE_N`) — and its own first rename destroyed that shape, which is why typing `Health Score` one key at a time left the API name at `h`.

#7819 replaced that with a **recorded owner** (`'label'` while the derivation owns the name, `'author'` the moment anyone types in the API name box), which is the posture `CreateViewDialog`'s `nameTouched` and `useCreateDerive`'s `touched` set already use.

⚠️ But the ruling's **second** boundary — *lock it on first save* — is still enforced by the placeholder-shape check, **because that is the only save signal this inspector can see**.

## The residual, stated precisely

The record deliberately does **not** end at the 1.5 s draft auto-save (`useDraftAutoSave`) — and that choice is forced, not sloppy: if the auto-save counted as "saved", per-keystroke sync would be **impossible by construction** (the first auto-save would fire mid-typing and freeze the name).

⇒ The window that stays open is narrow and exactly one shape:

> **the same mounted inspector session in which the field was created**, where a label edit *after* an auto-save still moves the API name.

Outside that window the behaviour is correct, and this is measured, not assumed:

| state | behaviour |
|:--|:--|
| new field, author has not touched the API name | syncs on every label change ✅ (this is the fix) |
| author has typed in the API name box | locked ✅ — **including** when what they typed is *shaped* like a placeholder (a hand-typed `field_9`, which no string pattern-match can distinguish from `nextFieldName()` output) |
| a published or reloaded field | locked ✅ — fresh mount, no record, non-placeholder name |
| **new field, same mount, after an auto-save** | ⬅ **still syncs — this card** |

## Why it needs a decision rather than a patch

Closing it requires the host to tell the inspector **"this field is persisted"** — a new prop on `MetadataInspectorProps`. That is a widening of a published props surface ⇒ **Clause-② `yes`**, and therefore not something the `domain:ui` dispatch lane takes on its own.

⚠️ It is also not obviously worth the prop. The residual only bites an author who, inside one uninterrupted inspector session, lets the draft auto-save fire and *then* keeps editing the label — and in that case the name following the label is arguably still the behaviour they want. ⇒ The real question is **whether the window is a defect at all**, and that is a ruling, not an implementation.

Related: objectui#7615 (the fix and the three pinned boundaries) · PR objectui#7819 · objectui#2260 (the original "API name follows the label until first save" ruling)
